recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-26314 unless the work group later reopens broader X-Provenance transaction Bundle behavior, which is outside this issue's accepted audit clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-26314 was a Published security work group change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking how to audit a PUT/POST request that includes the X-Provenance header. The accepted resolution was to add a Provenance HTTP Header bullet that one AuditEvent may be used to record creation of both the resource and the provenance.
initial_application: The X-Provenance header section was introduced by FHIR-19298 in commit eeeb015442e1adcf1c4e17ee2d7996e70d7f762c. FHIR-26314 was applied in commit 13f144d4c4aa36c0dc9136733bfbf525ab417ab5, adding the AuditEvent bullet to source/provenance/provenance-notes.xml. Commit 87b00c9c0de977f8559e0f99694e8664e03a06cd later capitalized the modal verb to MAY without changing the meaning.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists provenance=Provenance, so source/provenance/provenance-notes.xml is in current build scope. The linked Zulip thread supplies the rationale for a single server-generated AuditEvent that records both the resource create/update and the X-Provenance-created Provenance. Later FHIR-31345 was Resolved - No Change for transaction Bundle questions, and FHIR-34343 addressed version-specific transaction references separately; neither requires changing this audit bullet.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active source already says: When recording an AuditEvent, one AuditEvent MAY be used to record the create of the resource and provenance.
